title: Relative component-site equivalence over a geometric field
statement: Let X be affine, Ω algebraically closed, η:Spec Ω→X any map, and U→X an affine pro-etale object whose global-ring map is ind-etale across the fixed universes [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra]. Put V=U×_X Spec Ω, S=π₀(U), Q=π₀(V), and r:Q→S. Use the canonical component geometric morphisms π_U,π_V of [def-zl-generic-component-data]. Then π_V inverse image is an equivalence. There is a natural isomorphism r⁻¹⋙π_V⁻¹≅π_U⁻¹⋙g⁻¹, where r⁻¹ is the actual slice overMapPullback and g is the first projection [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. There is also a natural isomorphism q_Q⁻¹⋙π_V⁻¹≅p_Ω⁻¹⋙h⁻¹ for the second projection h:V→Spec Ω, where p_Ω inverse image is the fixed profinite point pullback [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point]. No genericity, irreducibility, or w-contractibility is assumed.

Its geometric characterization gives a map to the explicit component scheme. It is a homeomorphism with isomorphic stalk maps, hence a scheme isomorphism; coordinate uniqueness proves naturality.

proof.text: For an affine weakly etale scheme over the algebraically closed field, use the proved affine classification and stalk-isomorphism lemmas of GeometricFieldProfiniteDenseSubsite. The source and target spaces are totally disconnected. The component universal property therefore identifies every affine pro-etale object over the fibre with the component object on its actual connected components. Prove the component functor full and faithful by its coordinate universal property. Affine cover density and the finite jointly surjective refinement criterion prove it is a dense subsite, so restriction and its left adjoint are equivalences.

proof.text: For any morphism f:V→T between affine schemes, explicitly construct the map from the component object indexed by E×_π₀(T)π₀(V) to T_E. Use the component universal property to prove that its square over f is a pullback. Coordinate uniqueness gives naturality in E. Transfer this isomorphism to the canonical generic component functors, form the resulting isomorphism of composite sheaf direct images, and take adjunction mates.

proof.text: For affine T, the relative profinite test object T[S] and the component object on π₀(T)×S represent the same maps, using the label bijection and the component universal property. Construct inverse maps preserving the structure and label projections; uniqueness proves their inverse laws and naturality. Transfer to the canonical functor and take adjunction mates using the specified point adjunction. Compose with the existing point inverse-image composition isomorphism for V→Spec Ω. All constructions allow empty objects.
